one_liner: Cortex-M4F assembly-optimized ML-KEM and ML-DSA (plus other PQC schemes) that run 1.25-2.1x faster than PQClean clean C.
what_it_does: A collection of post-quantum KEM and signature implementations for the ARM Cortex-M4 plus the test, test-vector, speed, stack, hashing-profile and code-size harness used to compare them on a development board. Each scheme ships several variants side by side (clean from PQClean, m4f/m4fspeed for speed, m4fstack for low stack), all behind the NIST/SUPERCOP/PQClean API (crypto_kem_keypair/enc/dec, crypto_sign_keypair/crypto_sign/crypto_sign_open). You use it by copying one implementation directory plus the shared symmetric code into your firmware.
how_it_is_fast: The NTT and pointwise multiplication are hand-written ARMv7E-M assembly using the DSP halfword SIMD instructions (smulwb, smlabt, pkhtb, uadd16, usub16) and the improved Plantard modular multiplication of IACR ePrint 2022/956 (ML-KEM m4fspeed), with FPU s-registers used as extra storage for twiddle factors (vmov), which is why the variants are named m4f. ML-KEM fuses on-the-fly sampling of the public matrix with the matrix-vector product (matacc_asm.S, matacc_cache32/matacc_opt32 reuse cached products of the secret vector); ML-DSA m4f uses a 32-bit assembly NTT plus a small NTT modulo 769 (smallntt_769.S) for products with the short secret and challenge polynomials. Keccak is a shared XKCP-derived assembly permutation used by every variant, clean included.
when_to_use: Shipping ML-KEM-512/768/1024 on a Cortex-M4F microcontroller (STM32F4/L4 class) where KeyGen/Encaps/Decaps latency matters: ml-kem-768 m4fspeed decapsulates in about 708k cycles vs 1.39M for clean C.
Stack-constrained ML-KEM: ml-kem-768 m4fstack needs about 2.8-2.9 KB of stack (clean 10-14.5 KB) and is within 1% of m4fspeed's speed.
Firmware or certificate signature checks on an M4F: ml-dsa-44 m4f verifies in about 1.42M cycles with 8.9 KB of stack vs 2.06M cycles and 36 KB for clean.
Benchmarking a new Cortex-M4 PQC implementation against established numbers with the same speed/stack/hashing/size harness and board.
when_not_to_use: You need a maintained, audited product library: the README carries a deprecation notice (archive in or after January 2027) and points to mlkem-native and mldsa-native; the PQClean code behind the clean baseline was itself archived in August 2026.

Targets other than Cortex-M4F: the code uses ARMv7E-M DSP instructions and FPU registers, ml-dsa's ntt.S warns it must never be built for Cortex-M3 (UMULL is not constant time there); use PQRV for RISC-V or neon-ntt for Armv8-A.

ML-DSA signing on RAM-tight parts: ml-dsa-44 m4f needs about 38 KB of stack for KeyGen and 45 KB for Sign; the m4fstack variant fits in about 5 KB but signs slower than clean C (12.1M vs 7.9M cycles average).
Flash-bound designs: ml-kem-768 m4fspeed .text is 16,016 bytes vs 5,120 for clean, and ml-dsa-44 m4f is 19,592 vs 8,212.
You need power/EM side-channel or fault countermeasures: masking is not documented; the goal is speed, stack and constant-time code.

integration.dependencies: pqm4/mupq shared symmetric code (mupq/common/fips202.c plus common/keccakf1600.S, optionally sha2 and AES) and a randombytes() provider; libopencm3, OpenOCD/stlink and pyserial only for the board harness
integration.min_toolchain: arm-none-eabi-gcc with GNU assembler syntax (numbers taken with Arm GNU Toolchain 11.3.Rel1, 11.3.1 20220712), C gnu99, Python 3.8+ for the harness
integration.platforms: ARM Cortex-M4F (ARMv7E-M with FPv4-SP FPU); harness boards NUCLEO-L4R5ZI (default), STM32F4 Discovery, NUCLEO-L476RG, CW308T-STM32F3, MPS2-AN386 (QEMU, cycle counts meaningless there)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the functions work on caller buffers and the stack, and the only global (hash_cycles) exists for hash-profiling builds
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same crypto_kem_*/crypto_sign_* API and test vectors as the PQClean clean code (whose symbols carry a PQCLEAN_..._CLEAN_ prefix), but it only builds for Cortex-M4F

gotchas: The 'clean C' baseline is not pure portable C: mk/crypto.mk links the same assembly Keccak (common/keccakf1600.S) into every implementation, clean included. The hashing table shows Keccak costs the same cycles in both columns (ml-kem-768 KeyGen about 479k of 989k clean vs 478k of 642k m4fspeed), so outside hashing the M4 code is about 3.1x (KeyGen) to 4.1x (Decaps) faster for ml-kem-768 and 2.5-3.5x for ml-dsa-44 (derived from page data); the end-to-end 1.25-2.1x across ML-KEM and ML-DSA is capped by shared Keccak.
ML-DSA signing time is dominated by rejection sampling: ml-dsa-44 m4f Sign ranges from 1.81M to 17.0M cycles (average 3.94M over 1000 runs), so budget for the tail, not the average.

Licensing is per file, there is no top-level LICENSE file: the README dual-licenses non-implementation code under Apache-2.0 or CC0, but ml-dsa-44/m4f/smallntt_769.S carries an Apache-2.0-only header (Junhao Huang, 2023) while ntt.S is CC0 by permission; check headers before treating a directory as CC0.

Implementations are research code of uneven review: open issue #404 reports BIKE m4f with its Fujisaki-Okamoto constant-time protections commented out. Issue #411 (swapped polyveck_make_hint arguments, 'all signatures fail') names crypto_sign/dilithium2/m4fspeed, a path absent from master; master ml-dsa-44/m4f/sign.c passes (w0, w1) in the reference order, and ml-kem m4fspeed compress/tomsg already use the KyberSlash-safe multiply-shift instead of division.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick pqm4 when the target is a Cortex-M4F microcontroller: neon-ntt covers Armv8-A Neon (Cortex-A72, Apple M1) and PQRV covers RV32/RV64 cores for the same Kyber/Dilithium arithmetic. aadomn/aes is complementary rather than competing: it is the bitsliced constant-time AES that pqm4's common/aes.h already uses.
verified_claims_summary: benchmarks.md (ML-KEM rows added 2024-11-28 over 10 runs, ML-DSA rows updated 2025-02-10 over 1000 runs) reports SysTick-derived cycle counts on a NUCLEO-L4R5ZI at 24 MHz, built with arm-none-eabi-gcc 11.3.Rel1 at -O3 -g3 with identical -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mfloat-abi=hard -mfpu=fpv4-sp-d16 flags for clean and optimized variants. ml-kem-768 m4fspeed beats PQClean clean by 1.54x/1.73x/1.96x on KeyGen/Encaps/Decaps and ml-dsa-44 m4f by 1.31x/2.01x/1.45x on KeyGen/Sign/Verify (derived from page data), with both columns sharing the same assembly Keccak.
status_note: Commits continue (last 2026-09-04), but issue #409 (2026-08-22) deprecates pqm4: final pull requests by 30 November 2026 and archive in or after January 2027, with a volunteer co-maintainer invited on 2026-08-31; the per-scheme source is copyable under Apache-2.0 or CC0 apart from files with their own headers.
